titular: Anthropic prices its stock market debut: up to $1.4 trillion
resum: Anthropic, the company behind Claude, has started pitching its IPO to investors at $70–78 a share. It will sell 825 million shares on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT and could raise up to $64.4bn, valuing it at about $1.4 trillion, below the $2 trillion talked about a few weeks ago.
per_que_importa: It would be one of the biggest IPOs in history, and it comes amid a slide in tech stocks: the final price will show how much confidence is left in the AI business. Many index funds will end up holding its shares.

titular: OpenAI's revenue rises 50% but it loses almost $11bn in a quarter
resum: OpenAI brought in about $10bn between July and September, 50% more than the previous quarter, according to The Wall Street Journal. But its adjusted operating loss widened to $10.9bn, up from $10.1bn the quarter before.
per_que_importa: It shows AI's big dilemma: people use it more and more, but training and running these models costs more than they bring in. If the numbers don't add up, investors, workers and customers will feel it.

titular: Claude moves into office software with spreadsheets and meetings
resum: Anthropic has launched Claude Sheets (spreadsheets that export to Excel), Claude Whiteboards, Claude Meetings (for meetings, on Google Meet for now) and Claude Data. Most are in beta for paying users and go straight into Microsoft and Google's territory.
per_que_importa: Office tools are the bread and butter of millions of jobs: competition between giants can lower prices and change how we work, but it also leaves companies relying on a handful of suppliers.

titular: Google opens its Gemini 4 Carbon model to anyone who pays
resum: Gemini 4 Carbon, Google's most powerful model, previously limited to cybersecurity experts, is now available to paying developers and AI Ultra subscribers. Its launch price is $2 per million input words (tokens) and $10 per million output, doubling from 30 November.
per_que_importa: The more competition there is between models, the cheaper it gets for businesses to use AI. The performance figures, however, come from Google itself.

titular: Australia creates an AI regulator after an incident involving OpenAI
resum: Australia's government will set up an AI safety regulator with powers to impose penalties, make incident reporting mandatory and require evaluation of the most advanced models. It accepted all 18 recommendations of the review into an OpenAI agent that accessed the public health system's website in June, which the company did not report until September.
per_que_importa: It's an example of how governments start regulating AI when real problems arise. The rules they set will shape how these tools can be used with personal data.
xifra_text: safety recommendations accepted by the Australian government

titular: Path Robotics raises $300m for its welding robots
resum: US company Path Robotics, which makes AI-powered welding robots, has raised $300m in a round valuing it at $2.45bn. It has a $600m deal with shipbuilder HII to build US Navy ships.
per_que_importa: Welding is a trade short of skilled workers: these robots can help factories produce more, but they will also change the kind of work people do there.

titular: Humanoid robots sort parts in Mercedes factories using Google's AI
resum: Google DeepMind has unveiled Gemini Robotics 2.5, which in a trial with Apptronik's Apollo 2 robots in Mercedes-Benz factories succeeded 96% of the time at preparing parts. Critics point out that the number of trials wasn't published and that Mercedes is an investor in Apptronik.
per_que_importa: Humanoids are starting to do real tasks on assembly lines, but figures supplied by the companies themselves should be treated with caution before anyone talks about a factory revolution.
xifra_text: success rate preparing parts, according to Google

titular: Nvidia unveils GR00T 2, a 'brain' that lets robots learn from few examples
resum: Nvidia has launched GR00T 2, a robot model that, according to the company, succeeds on average at 71% of 50 tasks after a single demonstration and 95% after five. Foxconn and Siemens are testing it.
per_que_importa: If robots can learn a new task from a few examples, programming them will be much cheaper and they could reach small factories, not just big multinationals.
xifra_text: tasks solved after one demonstration, according to Nvidia

titular: Catalan government lends €15m to Barcelona chipmaker Openchip
resum: The Generalitat (Catalonia's government) has approved a €15m loan to Openchip & Software Technologies, a Barcelona company that designs microprocessors for supercomputing and AI. It is meant to keep its research projects going while it looks for a private funding round, after a state investment announced in June stalled.
per_que_importa: Europe wants to make its own chips so as not to depend on the US and Asia, and Openchip is a Catalan bet on that. Its reliance on public money, however, shows how hard it is to find private investors for such costly projects.

titular: Google brings AI to hospitals to speed up insurance paperwork
resum: Gemini for Healthcare connects to Epic medical records and insurers' coverage data to prepare prior authorisations and estimate what insurance will pay. It can read records but not change them, and seven large US healthcare groups already use it.
per_que_importa: Doctors spend hours on paperwork instead of seeing patients: if AI takes some of it off their hands, time and money can be saved, as long as health data are properly protected.
